title: Knowledge-enhanced Black-box Attacks for Recommendations

problem.claim: Attackers seek to inject crafted fake user profiles into recommender systems to promote or demote target items, with black-box attacks being more practical because target architecture, parameters, and training data are difficult to access.

gap.claim: Generating high-quality fake user profiles under black-box conditions is challenging when attackers have limited resources.

contributions.claim: A knowledge graph-enhanced black-box attacking framework, KGAttack, integrates item knowledge graphs into hierarchical policy networks.
KGAttack uses deep reinforcement learning to learn attacking policies that generate fake user profiles for adversarial black-box attacks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce a novel strategy that leverages publicly accessible item attribute information and knowledge graphs to enhance fake user profile generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that comprehensive experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of KGAttack under the black-box setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks involving injected fake user profiles.
Black-box attacks are more practical because attackers generally cannot access target-system architecture, parameters, or training data.
Limited access and resources make high-quality fake profile generation difficult.
The proposed KGAttack framework uses item knowledge graphs and hierarchical deep-reinforcement-learning policy networks to generate fake profiles.
Experiments on various real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate effectiveness in the black-box setting.

source_observation.claim: Publicly accessible item attribute information is integrated into hierarchical policy networks for black-box attack-profile generation.

interpretation.claim: Auxiliary domain knowledge may compensate for limited direct access to a target system.

application.claim: In other constrained black-box settings, consider incorporating publicly available structured knowledge into policy learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond recommender systems or different knowledge-graph availability conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, attack metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement-learning training procedure or resource requirements.
The abstract does not report limitations, robustness conditions, or independent verification.
